Bug_Title: "equals" methods should be symmetric and work for subclasses
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the equals method of the Fruit class. It uses a hardcoded class name (Fruit.class) in the comparison, which breaks the method for subclasses. This violates the symmetry principle of the equals contract.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when the 'equals' method of the Fruit class doesn't correctly handle subclasses. When a Fruit object is compared to a Raspberry object, it should return true if they are equal, but this is not the case because the Fruit class only checks if the object is an instance of Fruit, not its subclasses.
